title: प्रत्याहारसूत्राणांं समीक्षणात्मकमध्ययनम्
nepali: वेदस्य षट्ष्वङ्गेषु व्याकरणम् शरीरस्य मुखमिव मुख्यमस्ति । वेदार्थपरिज्ञानाय च व्याकरणमध्येयंवर्तते । तत्राचार्यस्य पाणिनेः अष्टाध्यायी नामकः सूत्रात्मकः व्याकरणविषयकः ग्रन्थः कालजयी परिपूर्णःस्फुटतरश्च विराजते । अइउण्, ऋलृक् इत्यादीनि चतुर्दश माहेश्वरसूत्राणि पाणिनीयव्याकरणस्याधारभूतानिउपजीव्यभूतानि विद्यन्ते । एभिः सूत्रैः प्रत्याहाराणाम् निर्माणं भवति । प्रत्याहारो नाम वर्णसंक्षेपः विद्यते ।प्रत्याहाराश्च पाणिनीयसूत्राणामाधारः वर्तते । यथा – इको यणचि (पा.सू.६।१।७७) अत्र प्रत्याहारौ इक् (इ,उ,ऋ,लृ, ) यण् (य,व,र,ल) इति । वर्णसमाम्नाय नाम्ना चैतानि ज्ञायन्ते । एतानि सूत्राणि पाणिनियानिपाणिनिप्रणीतानि सन्ति । पाणिनीयव्याकरणशास्त्रानुशासनस्य प्राणभूतानीमानि सूत्राणि प्राचीनवाङ्मयेषुऋक्प्रातिशाख्ये भाष्यादौ च वेदवत् ब्रह्मराशिरूपेण समादृतानि प्राप्यन्ते । प्रत्याहाराश्च पाणिनीयसूत्रेषुप्रतिसूत्रं राजन्ते । सूत्रेष्वन्तर्भूताः द्वाचत्वारिंशत् (४२) प्रत्याहाराः लभ्यन्ते । तदितरं कात्यानकृतेषु वार्तिकेषुच प्रत्याहाराणामुपयोगो विहितो विद्यते । काशिकाकारादयस्त्वेनं गोपर्वते पाणिनिकृतेन तपासा प्रसन्नस्यमहेश्वरस्य ढक्कानादात् पाणिनिना सूत्राणि प्राप्तानि सन्तीति निगदन्ति । महेश्वरवरप्रसादात्ढक्कानादोद्भवानि सूत्राणि समाख्याय पाणिनिः व्याकरणशास्त्रं प्रणिनाय इति च प्रसिद्धिरस्ति । अस्मिन्नालेखेसूत्राणां परिचयोपस्थानपूर्वकं प्रत्याहाराणां संख्यायाश्च निदर्शनं क्रियते । इमानि सूत्राणि पाणिनीयानि उतअपाणिनीयानि (माहेश्वराणीति) वस्तुसत्यमुपस्थाप्य ववेचनं विहितमस्ति । पाणिनीयेषु सूत्रेषु प्रयुक्तानांप्रत्याहाराणां संख्या च सदैव विवेचनस्य विषयभूतो विद्यते ।
american_english: Among the six limbs of the Veda, grammar is primary, just as the face is to the body. And for thoroughly understanding the meaning of the Vedas, grammar must be studied. In that regard, the aphoristic grammatical work named Ashtadhyayi by Acharya Panini stands as timeless, complete, and exceptionally clear. The fourteen Maheshvara Sutras, such as a-i-u-n, ri-lri-k, and so on, constitute the foundational and sustaining basis of Paninian grammar. By means of these sutras, pratyaharas (abbreviated phonetic groups) are formed. A pratyahara is indeed an abbreviation of phonemes. And pratyaharas are the foundation of the Paninian sutras. For example: iko yanaci (Panini Sutra 6.1.77), where the two pratyaharas are ik (i, u, ri, lri) and yan (y, v, r, l). And these are also known by the name Varnasammamnaaya (traditional catalogue of sounds). These sutras are Paninian, composed by Panini. Being the very lifeblood of the grammatical discipline of Panini, these sutras are found revered like the Vedas in the form of Brahmarashi (the sacred storehouse of Vedic knowledge) in ancient literature such as the Rigveda-Pratishakhya and the Mahabhashya. And pratyaharas reign supreme across rule after rule in Panini’s sutras. Forty-two (42) pratyaharas contained within the sutras are obtained. In addition, the use of pratyaharas is also prescribed in the Varttikas composed by Katyayana. The authors of the Kashika and others, however, state that Panini obtained these sutras from the sound of the damaru drum of Lord Maheshvara, who was pleased by the penance performed by Panini on Mount Gopavarta. And it is well known that Panini composed the science of grammar after articulating the sutras that arose from the drumbeats through the boon and grace of Maheshvara. In this article, after presenting an introduction to the sutras, an illustration of the count of pratyaharas is provided. Presenting the objective reality as to whether these sutras are Paninian or non-Paninian (namely Maheshvara), a critical discussion has been carried out. And the count of pratyaharas employed in the Paninian sutras has always remained a subject of scholarly debate.

informal_english: Out of the six Vedangas, grammar is the most important one, just like the face of the body. And to properly understand the meaning of the Vedas, studying grammar is a must. There, Acharya Panini’s aphoristic grammar treatise called the Ashtadhyayi stands out as timeless, totally complete, and crystal clear. The fourteen Maheshvara Sutras, like a-i-u-n, ri-lri-k, and so on, are the real foundational building blocks of Paninian grammar. Pratyaharas (code-like sound abbreviations) are formed using these very sutras. A pratyahara basically means an abbreviation of speech sounds. And pratyaharas form the very bedrock of Panini's sutras. Take the rule iko yanaci (Panini Sutra 6.1.77) for instance, where the two pratyaharas are ik (i, u, ri, lri) and yan (y, v, r, l). These are also known by the name Varnasammamnaaya. These sutras are Paninian, authored by Panini himself. Serving as the very life of Paninian grammatical discipline, these sutras are respected just like the Vedas as a sacred Brahmarashi in ancient texts like the Rigveda-Pratishakhya and commentaries. And pratyaharas show up and rule the roost in almost every single one of Panini's sutras. You get forty-two (42) pratyaharas directly embedded within the sutras. Besides that, pratyaharas are also used in the Varttikas penned by Katyayana. But commentators like the authors of the Kashika say that Panini got these sutras from the beat of Lord Maheshvara’s damaru drum, after the Lord was pleased with Panini’s penance on Mount Gopavarta. And there's a well-known belief that Panini formulated the entire grammatical system after reciting the sutras that came from the drumbeats by the grace of Maheshvara. In this article, after giving a basic intro to the sutras, the exact number of pratyaharas is clearly shown. Laying out the actual facts on whether these sutras are Panini’s own or non-Paninian (that is, Maheshvara), a thorough discussion is done. And the exact number of pratyaharas used in Panini's sutras has always remained a hot topic for debate.
translator_notes: Original abstract composed in Sanskrit. Strict clause and sentence order maintained. Phonetic examples, technical grammatical terms (pratyahara, Maheshvara Sutras, Varnasammamnaaya), and numbers (42) transliterated into Latin script to preserve clarity and prevent script leakage.
